newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to propose bank reforms next June.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to propose bank reforms next June.

text.p: Japan's influential advisory panel to the finance minister will finalise its proposals over steps to deregulate the financial markets next June, a member of the panel said on Tuesday.

Keimei Kaizuka, professor at Chuo University and a key member for the Financial System Research Council, told reporters the panel would soon summarise its discussions so far and then look at specific issues at the beginning of next year. "We will issue final proposals by June," he said.

The Financial System Research Council, which focuses on Japan's banking policy, is one of the advisory panels which Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto created to help set details of his "Big Bang" plans to liberalise the nation's financial markets by 2001.

The Securities and Exchange Council, an advisory panel to the finance minister for the nation's securities market and industry, will also work out its proposals by next June, a member of the council recently said.
Kaizuka said that one of issues the panel will discuss will be the establishment of financial holding companies.
